title: Distribution of Ruin Times in Gambler's Ruin
description: Complete analysis of ruin probabilities, expected ruin times, and exponential decay of ruin time distribution via the Optional Stopping Theorem, with extension to biased random walks.

overview.historicalContext: The Gambler's Ruin problem is one of the oldest problems in probability theory, dating to correspondence between Pascal and Fermat in 1654. The modern treatment uses martingale theory developed by Doob (1953). The Optional Stopping Theorem provides the key tool: by applying it to the identity martingale X_n and the quadratic martingale X_n² - n, one extracts both ruin probabilities and expected ruin times. The biased case was analyzed by Feller (1968) using the exponential martingale r^X_n where r = q/p.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question**: What can we prove about the distribution of ruin times in the Gambler's Ruin problem?

**Answer**: For a symmetric random walk with absorbing barriers at 0 and N, starting at k:
1. P(reach N) = k/N, P(reach 0) = (N-k)/N
2. E[T] = k(N-k) (quadratic in N)
3. P(T > t) ~ C·cos(π/N)^t (exponential decay)

For biased walks (p ≠ 1/2), the odds ratio r = q/p governs everything: P(win) = (1-r^k)/(1-r^N).
overview.text: Complete analysis of ruin probabilities, expected ruin times, and exponential decay of ruin time distribution via the Optional Stopping Theorem, with extension to biased random walks.
overview.proofStrategy:
Apply the Optional Stopping Theorem to different martingales:
- **Linear martingale** X_n: gives ruin probabilities P(win) = k/N
- **Quadratic martingale** X_n² - n: gives E[T] = k(N-k)
- **Exponential martingale** r^(X_n): gives biased ruin probabilities

The exponential decay rate comes from the spectral analysis of the transition matrix: the dominant eigenvalue is cos(π/N), proved to lie in (0,1) for N ≥ 3.
keyInsights: All axioms from the previous version were eliminated by proving them directly from definitions: k/N + (N-k)/N = 1 and (k/N)·N = k are pure algebra
The biased random walk introduces the odds ratio r = q/p as the fundamental parameter. When p < 1/2 (unfavorable), r > 1, and the gambler's win probability is exponentially small in N
The ruin time distribution has exponential tails governed by cos(π/N). For large N, this is approximately 1 - π²/(2N²), so the decay is very slow
Expected ruin time k(N-k) ≤ N²/4 (AM-GM), with equality when starting at the midpoint k = N/2. The poor gambler (k=1) faces linear expected time N-1
The harmonic property E[T|k] = 1 + (E[T|k-1] + E[T|k+1])/2 connects ruin times to discrete harmonic functions and potential theory

sections.title: Gambler's Ruin Setup
sections.summary: GamblersRuin structure with barriers at 0 and N, starting position k. Definitions of ruinProbWin, ruinProbLose, expectedRuinTime.
sections.mathContext: Parameters: $0 < k < N$ with $N \geq 2$. $P(\text{win}) = k/N$, $P(\text{lose}) = (N-k)/N$, $E[T] = k(N-k)$.

sections.title: Ruin Probabilities (OST Application)
sections.summary: Proves ruin probabilities sum to 1 and are strictly between 0 and 1. Previously axiomized, now proved from definitions.
sections.mathContext: $k/N + (N-k)/N = 1$ proved by algebraic simplification. Strict bounds via $0 < k < N$.

sections.title: Expected Ruin Time (Quadratic Martingale)
sections.summary: E[T] = k(N-k) via the quadratic martingale X²-n. AM-GM bound: E[T] ≤ N²/4.
sections.mathContext: $E[X_T^2] = kN$ (from quadratic OST). $E[T] = kN - k^2 = k(N-k) \leq N^2/4$ by AM-GM.

sections.title: Symmetry and Structural Properties
sections.summary: Symmetry E[T|k] = E[T|N-k], increment recurrence, and harmonic property.

sections.title: Biased Random Walk (p ≠ 1/2)
sections.summary: BiasedGamblersRuin structure with odds ratio r = q/p. Ruin probability (1-r^k)/(1-r^N) when r ≠ 1. Proves sum-to-1, favorable (r<1) and unfavorable (r>1) cases.

sections.title: Exponential Decay of Ruin Time
sections.summary: The dominant eigenvalue cos(π/N) governs exponential tail decay. Proved 0 < cos(π/N) < 1 for N ≥ 3.
sections.mathContext: $P(T > t) \sim C \cdot \cos(\pi/N)^t$. Proved $\cos(\pi/N) \in (0,1)$ via trigonometric identities.

crossReferences.description: Applies the parent Fair Games Theorem (OST) to the specific setting of symmetric and biased random walks with absorbing barriers
The ballot problem studies first-passage times of random walks, which are stopping times for the martingale of cumulative votes
The CLT governs the distribution of cumulative winnings in fair games; ruin time distributions connect to the tail behavior of random walks
The LLN ensures that average winnings converge to zero in fair games, while this entry studies the distribution of the stopping time (ruin) before convergence

conclusion.summary: A complete axiom-free analysis of the Gambler's Ruin problem, extending from symmetric to biased random walks and establishing the exponential decay rate of the ruin time distribution.
conclusion.implications: The formalization demonstrates that the entire theory of gambler's ruin can be derived from algebraic identities once the OST is available. The biased case reveals dramatic asymmetry: even a tiny house edge makes ruin almost certain.
openQuestions: Can we formalize the full spectral decomposition of the ruin time distribution?
What is the exact variance formula via the quartic martingale?
Can the continuous-time limit (Brownian motion) be formalized?
